Fact definition: How and why key design choices in training were made.
Extracted value: The card gives limited rationale: a single merged model handles instruction-following, reasoning and coding in one set of weights (a unified model aimed at better performance than previous models), and the vision encoder was trained from scratch to handle variable image sizes and aspect ratios.
Quotes given as evidence (separated by [...]): Mistral Medium 3.5 is our first flagship merged model. It is a dense 128B model with a 256k context window, handling instruction-following, reasoning,
and coding in a single set of weights. [...] We trained the vision encoder from
scratch to handle variable image sizes and aspect ratios.

Grade the extraction:
- "y": the quotes are about this model and support every claim in the value, and the value answers the fact definition.
- "partial": mostly right, but the value adds claims the quotes don't support, drops an important qualifier, or only partly answers the definition.
- "n": wrong, unsupported, about a different model, or does not answer the definition.

answer.reason: Partly supported. The quotes back up two points: the model is merged so that instruction-following, reasoning and coding share one set of weights, and the vision encoder was trained from scratch to handle variable image sizes and aspect ratios. That second point gives a real "why." But the value also says the unified model was "aimed at better performance than previous models," and none of the quotes say that. The card does say this elsewhere, but it was left out of the evidence. The quotes give no reason for the merged design, so they only partly answer the "how and why" in the fact definition.
